# LOG-002: Proxy access logs are rotated

- **Group:** Logs and monitoring
- **Severity when it fails:** low
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

A reverse proxy access log grows with traffic and is never trimmed by the proxy itself. A log over 1 GiB with no logrotate rule is a future full disk. Only the usual /var/log locations of nginx, Caddy, Traefik, Apache and HAProxy are inspected; container logs are not.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls -lh /var/log/nginx /var/log/caddy /var/log/traefik; ls /etc/logrotate.d
```

## How to fix it

Add a logrotate rule (use copytruncate when the proxy cannot reopen its log).

## What a fix can break

copytruncate can lose a few lines written during the copy.

Run `stackward explain LOG-002` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
